approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Lifecycle stage and transition boundary
canonical_definition: The current lifecycle stage, permitted activities, target stage, acceptance criteria, evidence threshold, authorization boundary and rollback or retirement path are explicit and enforced from qualification through retirement.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system and to every requested or de facto lifecycle transition, including qualification, development, validation, deployment, operation, material expansion, suspension, rollback and retirement.
conditions: Identify the current lifecycle stage, requested target stage, system scope, environment, users, data, credentials, integrations, autonomy and permitted activities before relying on a stage label.
Define stage-specific acceptance criteria, required evidence, accountable owners, transition authority, expiry and rollback conditions before progression begins.
Enforce technical and operational separation between experiments and production, including data, credentials, access, integrations, infrastructure, users and decision consequences.

Treat accumulated real users, production data, persistent integrations, operational dependency or business-critical reliance as potential de facto progression requiring reassessment and authorization.
Maintain transition traceability, monitoring, rollback, suspension and retirement capability throughout the lifecycle.
exclusions: A project-management label, repository branch, environment name or vendor release label does not by itself establish the governed lifecycle stage.
Completion of development work, a successful demonstration or a model-quality result does not authorize deployment or production operation.
A temporary exception does not redefine the lifecycle stage unless its scope, authority, expiry, controls and reassessment route are formally approved.
reassessment_triggers: A new or expanded user group, affected population, customer, decision consequence or business dependency
Use of production, personal, confidential, regulated or representative operational data in an experiment or test environment
Introduction of production credentials, privileged access, live integrations, external APIs, automation or autonomous action
Material scale, availability, performance, cost, security, legal, provider, model, data or architecture change
Transition criteria, assumptions, evidence or approval expires, is contradicted or is bypassed
Incident, complaint, monitoring result or audit indicates boundary drift, hidden production use or loss of rollback capability
Suspension, rollback, redeployment, retirement or transfer to another owner or operating context

primary_questions.question: Are the current and target lifecycle stages, system scope, permitted and prohibited activities, transition criteria and accountable authorization boundary explicitly defined?
Are stage-specific environment, data, credential, access, user, integration and decision boundaries technically and operationally enforced, with rollback and retirement remaining possible?

Does current evidence demonstrate that transition criteria are met, the correct authority approved progression, boundary drift is detected and the system can be suspended, rolled back or retired safely?

required_evidence.title: Lifecycle stage and boundary record
required_evidence.claim_supported: The current governed stage, target stage, system version and boundary, permitted and prohibited activities, users, environments, data classes, integrations and decision consequences are explicitly recorded.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies the exact system version, component set, environment, owner, current stage, target stage and decision date.
Defines permitted and prohibited users, data, credentials, integrations, actions, scale, availability and external exposure for the current stage.
limitations: A project plan, backlog status, environment name or informal statement that the system is a pilot is insufficient.

required_evidence.title: Stage-specific technical and operational boundary evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Technical and operational controls enforce separation between experimental, validation and production contexts.
acceptance_conditions: Demonstrates distinct identities, credentials, access policies, secrets, data paths, infrastructure, integrations, logging and deployment controls for each material stage.
Shows that production users, data, credentials, live integrations and consequential actions cannot enter an earlier stage without an approved controlled path.
limitations: Documentation without configuration, access, deployment or runtime evidence does not establish enforcement.

required_evidence.title: Transition acceptance and evidence matrix
required_evidence.claim_supported: Each requested transition has predefined acceptance criteria, evidence requirements, assurance thresholds, unresolved-condition treatment and accountable owners.
acceptance_conditions: Criteria cover purpose, classification, value, roles, data, security, evaluation, human impact, operational readiness, monitoring and legal or contractual dependencies where applicable.
Criteria are defined before the transition decision and identify blocking, conditional and deferrable items.
limitations: Criteria created after deployment or tailored only to evidence already available cannot establish an independent gate.

required_evidence.title: Transition dossier and criteria results
required_evidence.claim_supported: The transition dossier demonstrates the result of every applicable acceptance criterion and links each conclusion to current evidence.
acceptance_conditions: Includes pass, fail, conditional, unknown and not-applicable outcomes with rationale, evidence IDs, owners and expiry.
Preserves unresolved conflicts and explicitly records constraints, remediation and reassessment conditions.
limitations: A summary statement that testing passed or risks are acceptable is insufficient without criterion-level traceability.

required_evidence.title: Lifecycle authorization and exception record
required_evidence.claim_supported: The correct accountable authority approves, rejects or conditionally authorizes the exact transition, scope, version and operating boundary.
acceptance_conditions: Names the decision authority, decision date, target stage, system version, permitted scope, conditions, expiry, residual-risk owner and rollback trigger.
Separates development approval, technical sign-off, business sponsorship, legal review and deployment authorization according to assigned authority.
limitations: Attendance, funding, project sponsorship, development completion or an unscoped email does not establish lifecycle authorization.

required_evidence.title: Boundary-drift and de facto progression monitoring
required_evidence.claim_supported: Monitoring detects real users, production data or credentials, live integrations, expanded scale, operational dependency and other indicators of de facto lifecycle progression.
acceptance_conditions: Uses technical telemetry, access records, integration inventory, data-flow evidence, usage records and ownership review rather than declarations alone.
Creates timely attributable cases, constraints and reassessment when a stage boundary is crossed or approached.
limitations: Absence of a reported incident or formal deployment event does not establish absence of boundary drift.

required_evidence.title: Rollback, suspension and retirement assurance
required_evidence.claim_supported: The system can be suspended, rolled back, bypassed or retired without unacceptable loss of safety, compliance, evidence, service continuity or downstream control.
acceptance_conditions: Defines decision thresholds, responsible authority, technical procedures, dependencies, data and record handling, communication and continuity arrangements.
Includes representative test or exercise evidence and records limitations, recovery time, irreversible dependencies and remediation.
limitations: A written rollback plan that has not been tested against representative dependencies cannot exceed IMPLEMENTED assurance.

required_evidence.title: Independent transition and lifecycle-control review
required_evidence.claim_supported: A competent reviewer independent from the delivery pressure challenges stage classification, criteria, evidence, exceptions, approval authority, drift controls and reversibility.
acceptance_conditions: Review independence and competence are appropriate to the consequence and target stage.
Material challenge, dissent, unresolved evidence and required constraints are recorded before progression.
limitations: A review performed by the same person who owns delivery evidence does not establish independent assurance.

evidence_ceilings: A lifecycle stage cannot exceed DECLARED assurance until the exact system, environment, users, data, integrations, permitted activities and target decision are identified.
A transition cannot exceed IMPLEMENTED assurance until stage-specific boundaries and acceptance criteria exist and are enforced.
Deployment or production progression cannot exceed TESTED assurance without criterion-level results and formal authorization for the exact version and scope.
Operational boundary effectiveness and rollback readiness cannot exceed OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED until representative runtime and exercise evidence exists.
Tactic completion, project status or model performance cannot authorize a lifecycle transition.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat a controlled pilot as production merely because real users participate when scope, data, access, consequences, approvals and exit conditions are explicitly bounded.
Do not treat shared infrastructure as boundary failure when isolation, access, data, credentials, logging and deployment controls are demonstrably effective.
Do not require every transition to use identical criteria; require proportionate, predefined and traceable criteria for the actual risk and target stage.
Do not treat a formally constrained exception as uncontrolled drift when authority, scope, expiry, monitoring and rollback are explicit and current.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer lifecycle stage from environment names, repository branches, project labels, contracts, user counts or vendor terminology alone.
Do not infer deployment authorization from development completion, technical validation, funding, sponsorship or absence of objection.
Do not infer transition readiness from a single aggregate score, model benchmark or successful demonstration.
Do not infer rollback capability from backups, version control or a written procedure without dependency-aware test evidence.
Do not clear a hard gate because remediation is planned or a tactic has been selected.
contradiction_handling: Observed users, data, credentials, integrations, availability or business dependency override a stale declared stage for present-state assessment.
Conflicting transition criteria, evidence or approvals keep the affected decision UNKNOWN and block or constrain progression until accountable adjudication.
Where technical configuration and approval records disagree, apply the more restrictive boundary and investigate potential de facto progression.
An exception that exceeds its scope or expiry is assessed as an uncontrolled boundary crossing, not as an approved continuation.
freshness_rules: Revalidate the lifecycle record before every requested transition and after every material change or de facto progression indicator.
Transition evidence and approvals are version-, scope-, environment- and time-specific and expire when dependencies or assumptions change.
Boundary-drift monitoring and rollback tests must be current for the operational dependency, scale and consequence of the system.
Retirement and continuity arrangements must be reviewed when downstream dependencies or owners change.

conditions: Block deployment, material expansion or consequential operation when the current or target lifecycle stage and permitted boundary are materially undefined.
Block transition when production data, credentials, users, integrations or consequential actions can cross into an earlier stage without an approved controlled path.
Block progression when applicable acceptance criteria, required evidence or independent review remain failed, conflicting or UNKNOWN without a formally approved constrained decision.
Block transition when the approving authority is absent, incorrect, expired or does not cover the exact system version, scope and target stage.
Block or constrain continued operation when boundary drift, hidden production dependency or loss of suspension, rollback or retirement capability is detected.

normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Requires continuous lifecycle risk management, documented quality and change-management procedures, reassessment after substantial modification, conformity decisions where applicable and post-market monitoring throughout the system lifetime.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core GOVERN 1.4-1.7 and 2.3; MAP 1.1; MANAGE 1.1 and 4.1; Effectiveness section on explicit go/no-go commissioning and deployment decisions
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Supports explicit lifecycle governance, inventory, monitoring, executive responsibility, go/no-go decisions, safe decommissioning and iterative management across design, development, deployment, operation and retirement.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Guidelines overview; Secure development - identify, track and protect assets and manage technical debt; Secure deployment - secure infrastructure and release AI responsibly; Secure operation and maintenance - monitoring and secure updates
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Defines lifecycle-specific secure design, development, deployment and operation practices, including environment segregation, access controls, responsible release, monitoring, updates and continued protection.

finding_definitions.title: Current stage, target stage or permitted lifecycle boundary is materially undefined
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block consequential progression until the exact system, current stage, target stage, permitted activities and accountable boundary are defined and human-validated.

finding_definitions.title: Stage-specific environment, data, credential, access, user or integration separation is ineffective
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block transition or constrain operation until the affected technical and operational boundary is enforced and tested.

finding_definitions.title: Transition acceptance criteria or criterion-level evidence is incomplete, retrospective or unresolved
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block the requested transition unless failed, conflicting or unknown criteria are resolved or explicitly bounded by the correct authority.

finding_definitions.title: Lifecycle transition lacks valid authorization for the exact version, scope and target stage
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Do not treat the transition as authorized; require attributable formal decision, independent challenge where needed and renewed evidence.

finding_definitions.title: Boundary-drift detection, rollback, suspension or retirement capability is ineffective
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain continued operation or expansion and require drift investigation, dependency reduction and tested recovery or retirement controls before further reliance.

machine_may: Extract lifecycle labels, environments, users, data classes, credentials, integrations, criteria, test results, approvals, exceptions, telemetry and change records.
Compare declared stage with technical and operational evidence and identify potential de facto progression, missing criteria, expired approvals and boundary contradictions.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible finding states for accountable human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Authorize, reject or conditionally approve a lifecycle transition.
Treat project status, model quality, deployment automation, sponsor intent or absence of incident as proof of stage or readiness.
Waive acceptance criteria, select residual-risk tolerance, extend an exception or redefine the governed boundary.
Clear a hard gate, lock a finding, accept residual risk or authorize continued operation, rollback, redeployment or retirement.
human_authority_required_for: Define the governed current and target lifecycle stage, permitted activities, acceptance criteria and authority model.
Determine whether evidence satisfies transition criteria and adjudicate conflicts, unknowns and exceptions.
Approve, reject, constrain, suspend, roll back, redeploy or retire the exact system version and operating scope.
Lock findings, accept residual risk and approve bounded exceptions with expiry and monitoring.
Determine whether observed use constitutes de facto progression and order corrective action.

governance_purpose: Ensure that every AI system remains inside an explicit, evidence-backed and authorized lifecycle boundary and cannot drift from experiment to consequential production use without reassessment, control and accountable approval.
distinct_claim: A5 owns the current lifecycle stage, stage-specific permitted boundary, transition acceptance criteria, transition evidence, authorization, rollback and retirement path. A1 owns intended purpose and use boundaries; A2 owns proportionality and value; A3 owns role and responsibility allocation; A4 owns risk, legal and regulatory classification and reclassification.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The exact system version, current lifecycle stage, requested target stage and transition scope are explicitly identified and current.
Permitted and prohibited users, data, credentials, integrations, environments, actions, scale, availability and decision consequences are defined for the current and target stages.
Stage-specific technical and operational controls enforce separation of environment, data, credentials, access, users, integrations, infrastructure and consequential actions.
Transition acceptance criteria, required evidence, assurance thresholds, owners, blocking conditions, expiry and rollback triggers are predefined and proportionate to the target stage.
The transition dossier records criterion-level results, evidence, unresolved conflicts, constraints and reassessment conditions for the exact version and scope.
The correct accountable authority approves, rejects or conditionally authorizes the exact transition, version, scope, conditions, expiry and residual-risk ownership.
Technical telemetry and governance review detect boundary drift and de facto progression through real users, production data or credentials, live integrations, scale or operational dependency.
Suspension, rollback, bypass and retirement procedures are dependency-aware, tested and capable of preserving required evidence, continuity and control.
A competent reviewer independent from delivery pressure challenges lifecycle classification, criteria, evidence, exceptions, authority and reversibility before consequential progression.
